title: VisitQuill
description: Prepare a focused appointment brief from selected health records. Organize questions, medications and results for your next visit with VisitQuill.
workflow: Prepare and download a personal appointment brief from selected authorized records.
subject: Appointment preparation & personal health briefs
label: Field notes for your next visit
headline: Why we chose to use FinchNode for VisitQuill
summary: The design decisions behind a consent-first appointment brief, from choosing record categories to keeping source details visible.
sections: VisitQuill has a narrow job: help someone choose the information they want to bring to an appointment. A record can contain much more than one visit needs. The interface therefore separates importing information from choosing talking points. It presents source details for review and lets the visitor download a selected brief. It does not decide which symptom matters most or suggest a treatment.
Why the connection is a separate step

We chose FinchNode for the connection layer implemented in VisitQuill because its Hosted Connect flow separates patient authorization from the brief-writing interface. The visitor chooses categories here, then continues to the source organization’s sign-in through the hosted flow. The browser does not receive our production API key. Our connection server requests the authorized snapshot and the app presents the selected information.
A useful brief needs its context

A medication name without source directions or a lab value without units can be a poor conversation aid. VisitQuill keeps supplied details with the items the visitor reviews. Missing categories and incomplete sync warnings remain visible. An empty section means information was not returned; it does not establish that there is nothing to discuss. Questions about an entry belong in the conversation with the care team.
A focused foundation for the product

Choosing a connection layer lets VisitQuill concentrate on the appointment experience: readable context, deliberate selection and a useful brief. The public repository makes these design choices inspectable. The site is deployed, while production activation is the next step before live imports become available. Connection and consent details are explained before a visitor authorizes access.
Take a brief you can explain

When a connection is available, review the imported details, choose the items you want to discuss, and download the brief deliberately. Keep a downloaded copy private. It is a snapshot: later record corrections or sharing revocation will not change that file. Bring your own questions alongside it, since a brief cannot replace the parts of your experience that never appeared in a record.
guideIntro: Prepare a focused appointment conversation: choose record-based talking points, understand what the downloaded brief contains, and keep a route back to the details.
finchnodeContext: VisitQuill uses FinchNode to bring authorized conditions, medications and lab observations into the selection workspace. Choosing what to discuss and creating the brief happen in VisitQuill; the connection does not choose a clinical priority for the visitor.

articles.title: How to prepare an appointment brief from your health records
articles.description: Turn selected conditions, medications and lab observations into a short appointment discussion list. Learn what VisitQuill includes in its text download.

sections.heading: Choose a question before choosing a record
paragraphs: A useful appointment brief starts with what you want to discuss. You might want help understanding a recorded label, checking whether an entry is still relevant, or finding the context behind a result. Keep those questions in your own notes; VisitQuill currently selects record labels rather than providing a free-text question editor.

sections.heading: Build your selection deliberately
paragraphs: After an authorized import becomes available, the workspace lists conditions, medications and lab observations. Select “Discuss at my visit” beside the entries you want to bring forward. The counter and numbered list show the current selection. Selecting an entry does not change the underlying health record.
items: Read the displayed record before selecting it.
Choose the entries connected to your planned conversation.
Review the numbered list and remove items you selected accidentally.

sections.heading: Understand the downloaded brief
paragraphs: “Download my brief” creates a text file of the selected labels. It is a talking-point list, not a full copy of the record: values, units, detailed directions and source documents are not all reproduced. If a detail matters to your question, keep access to the original information through the appropriate patient portal.

sections.heading: Finish with a readable list
paragraphs: Read the file before your appointment and add any personal questions using your own text editor. The app does not send the brief to a clinician or book a visit. Selections belong to the current session; a downloaded copy has its own lifetime. Live record connections still require production activation.

questions.question: Does the brief include every imported record?
questions.answer: No. It contains labels from the entries you select. The download button stays disabled until you choose at least one talking point.

questions.question: Can VisitQuill update my chart?
questions.answer: The implemented workflow is read-only. Selecting or downloading talking points does not edit a provider’s record.

articles.title: Why appointment topics and connection permissions are separate
articles.description: See how VisitQuill separates authorized record access from the talking points a visitor selects for an appointment brief.

sections.heading: Two choices with different effects
paragraphs: Approving a record connection determines which categories the application may receive. Checking a talking point determines which returned label goes into the appointment brief. These are separate controls: unchecking a topic is not a request to revoke sharing.

sections.heading: Keep the connection on the server
paragraphs: The source implementation starts a hosted connection through a separate server. That server requests the categories allowed for VisitQuill and returns to this site’s import workspace. Browser code does not contain the production API key. The visitor’s temporary session is bound to the exact site origin.

sections.heading: Keep the discussion list in the product
paragraphs: Once records are available, the interface maintains a selection of record IDs and derives the brief from those IDs. That makes the output inspectable: every talking point should correspond to a selected entry. The interface does not add recommendations, decide which condition is most important, or send the list elsewhere.

sections.heading: Make the boundary visible at handoff
paragraphs: A future operator should preserve this separation when extending VisitQuill. Adding a question editor need not broaden record access. Adding a new record category does require reviewing the actual authorization request and disclosures. The current public deployment documents the implemented flow; it is not evidence that a patient connection has been activated.

questions.question: Does removing a talking point revoke access?
questions.answer: No. It changes the brief selection. Use the sharing controls described in the privacy notice to manage the authorized connection.

finchnode.heading: The role of FinchNode in this design
finchnode.text: In VisitQuill’s implementation, FinchNode supplies the authorization handoff and records the server can request. VisitQuill supplies the appointment-specific selection and text output. The distinction keeps the explanation of the brief tied to what the visitor actually chose.
finchnode.label: FinchNode patient-authorized record connections

articles.title: How to build an appointment-brief app like VisitQuill
articles.description: Follow VisitQuill’s public GitHub code from a React interface to a server-side FinchNode connection, then build, test and deploy a focused health-record app.

sections.heading: Begin with a small output you can explain
paragraphs: VisitQuill turns selected condition, medication and lab-observation labels into a personal appointment brief. That is a deliberately small feature boundary. A developer can trace each downloaded line to a selected entry instead of starting with an open-ended attempt to summarize an entire medical history.

The public frontend repository contains the React interface, formatting helpers, content and tests. Read its README and license before adapting it for your own product. The source is an implementation reference; cloning it does not activate a patient connection.

sections.heading: Build the public interface first
paragraphs: The project uses React and Vite, with Node 22.13 or newer specified in its setup. Install dependencies, generate the static build and run the tests. Building before testing matters because the SEO checks inspect the generated files in dist.
The development command starts the local interface. Keep its public pages separate from the private import route, /#/import. A visitor reading a guide should not start a record request.
sections.code:
git clone https://github.com/visitquill/app.git
cd app
npm ci
npm run build
npm test
npm run dev

sections.heading: Trace the brief through the actual component
paragraphs: In app/view.tsx, selected stores record IDs. The component derives chosen entries from that selection, displays their labels and enables the download once at least one entry is selected. The text output is built from those labels.

To customize the product, start at this boundary. A notes field, a different brief layout or a clearer selection experience can be implemented in the product without pretending that the connection itself generated clinical advice.

sections.heading: Put the FinchNode connection behind a server
paragraphs: The separate Node service creates the hosted FinchNode connection session, checks its status and retrieves categories granted to that session. The frontend talks to that service; the production API key stays in the server’s environment. The server binds temporary access to the exact site origin.

A business adapting the application should operate its own approved configuration. Review the domain-to-site mapping, category allowlist, return URL and frontend Content-Security-Policy together. Merely deploying a copy of the static frontend does not create an independent connection service.

sections.heading: Test the boundaries before enabling connections
paragraphs: The frontend tests cover record formatting, public page discovery and search. The backend’s injected mock tests exercise origin restrictions, scope and session behavior without requiring real medical records. Use those tests to understand the contract before extending it.
items: Confirm that unsupported categories are rejected by the server.
Keep missing source fields visible rather than filling them with examples.
Check ended sessions and failed authorization, not only a successful response.
Keep all private workspace routes out of the sitemap.

sections.heading: Deploy the product and complete the operator setup
paragraphs: For the static frontend, the documented Render build is npm ci && npm run build with dist as the publish directory. The Node connection service is a separate deployment. A new business must align its registered FinchNode application, purpose, privacy details, server secrets and allowed origin before enabling patient use.

Keep the business’s canonical domain in content/seo.json and add future guides there. The build generates the searchable guide index, related links and sitemap. VisitQuill’s current public site is live, but its patient connection remains pending operator activation.

questions.question: Is the website and the connection service one deployment?
questions.answer: No. VisitQuill is a static frontend; its authorized connection runs through a separate Node server.

questions.question: Can I put a FinchNode API key in a Vite variable?
questions.answer: No. Frontend build variables can be shipped to the browser. Keep production credentials in the backend secret environment.

articles.title: Best AI medical scribes for small practices in 2026
articles.description: Ambient AI scribes a small practice can actually buy, from Freed and Heidi to EHR-built-in options, with published prices, trial evidence and a pre-purchase checklist.

sections.heading: What an ambient scribe does, and what the evidence shows
paragraphs: An ambient AI scribe listens to a visit, with the patient’s permission, and drafts a clinical note for the clinician to review and sign. The clinician remains responsible for the note. The appeal for a small practice is time: fewer evenings finishing charts.

The evidence is encouraging but mixed. In a randomized trial of 238 UCLA physicians published in NEJM AI, one scribe reduced time in notes by about 9.5% compared with usual care, while the other did not show a statistically significant change; both improved a burnout survey score. A JAMA Network Open study of 263 clinicians using Abridge across six health systems reported burnout falling from 51.9% to 38.8%. Results depend on the product and how it is rolled out.

links.label: Lukac et al., NEJM AI randomized trial
Olson et al., JAMA Network Open

sections.heading: The shortlist at a glance
paragraphs: Many well-known scribes are sold only to health systems. This ranking favors products a practice of one to ten clinicians can evaluate without an enterprise contract.

sections.heading: 1. Freed — quickest start for a solo clinician
paragraphs: Freed publishes its pricing: Starter at $39 a month for one clinician and 40 notes, Core at $79 a month with unlimited notes, and Premier at $119 monthly or $104 a month billed annually, which adds pushing notes into any browser-based EHR plus ICD-10 and CPT suggestions. There is a seven-day free trial.

Freed says it does not store patient recordings. Its Groups plan lists an organization-wide business associate agreement; if you are on an individual plan, confirm the BAA arrangement before recording real visits.

sections.heading: 2. Heidi Health — a free way to try ambient notes
paragraphs: Heidi offers a free plan with unlimited ambient documentation and a Clinician plan at $110 per user per month billed annually, with a 14-day trial. EHR integration is listed on its custom-priced Teams plan. Heidi states that it executes business associate agreements.

sections.heading: 3. The scribe built into your EHR
paragraphs: If your EHR has its own scribe, it deserves a trial before a separate product. Notes land in the chart without copying, and the vendor already holds your patient data. athenaOne includes athenaAmbient at no additional charge; eClinicalWorks sells Sunoh.ai; CharmHealth lists an AI Scribe at $125 per provider per month or $2 per encounter; DrChrono offers EverHealth Scribe; and Cerbo lists an AI scribe from $29 a month.
The trade-off is choice. A built-in scribe ties your documentation workflow to the EHR, and quality varies between vendors.

sections.heading: 4. Nabla — broad EHR integrations
paragraphs: Nabla reports more than 85,000 clinicians across more than 130 organizations and lists integrations with Epic, athenahealth, Oracle Health, NextGen and Greenway. It does not publish pricing. It publishes terms that include a business associate agreement, which users subject to HIPAA must accept.

sections.heading: 5. Microsoft Dragon Copilot — for practices tied to a health system
paragraphs: Dragon Copilot, which succeeded DAX, is aimed at physicians, nurses and radiologists and integrates with Epic. Microsoft does not publish pricing. It is most practical for practices whose affiliated health system already licenses it.

Other enterprise scribes, including Abridge, Suki, Ambience, Commure and DeepScribe, are strong products sold mainly to health systems or specific specialties. DeepScribe, for example, started in oncology.

sections.heading: Check these before recording a real visit
paragraphs: A two-week pilot with a few clinicians will tell you more than any comparison article.
items: Get a signed business associate agreement that covers the plan you are actually on.
Decide how you will ask patients for permission to record, and check your state’s recording-consent rules.
Find out whether audio is stored, for how long, and whether transcripts are used to improve the product.
Read every draft before signing; watch for invented findings, missed negatives and wrong medication doses.
Audit any suggested billing codes against the documented visit.
Measure time spent on notes before and after the pilot rather than relying on impressions.

questions.question: Is a free AI scribe safe to use with real patients?
questions.answer: Only if the vendor signs a business associate agreement covering that plan and you are comfortable with its data handling. Check the plan terms, not just the marketing page.

questions.question: Do AI scribes reduce burnout?
questions.answer: Published studies report improvements in burnout and documentation time, but effects vary by product and setting. Run your own pilot and measure it.

articles.editorialNote: How we ranked: published pricing, product and policy pages reviewed on September 28, 2026, and peer-reviewed studies linked in each section. Products were not tested hands-on.

articles.title: Best website development agencies for dentists (2026)
articles.description: Compare website development agencies for dentists. Our unpaid Cider recommendation, specialist alternatives, pricing context and a practical hiring checklist.
articles.editorialNote: Unpaid publisher recommendation: this site’s publisher recently used Cider Websites and liked the experience. Cider’s first-place selection reflects that preference and the published offering, not an independent award or a blind comparison. The publisher is not being paid for this article. Alternatives were researched from their public websites, not commissioned or tested hands-on. “Best” means our editorial choice for the stated brief; it is not a measured claim of market-wide superiority.

sections.heading: What a website for dentists needs
paragraphs: VisitQuill focuses on appointment preparation. Dental websites contribute earlier in the same journey by explaining services, introducing the team and helping people request a visit. These are our website-development picks for small dental practices, with emphasis on useful patient information and a manageable launch.

A patient should be able to find the practice, understand the type of care offered and see how appointment requests work. New-patient instructions, payment information and the difference between routine inquiries and urgent calls should be easy to scan. Request confirmation is a distinct step from a confirmed appointment.

sections.heading: Our shortlist and selection criteria
paragraphs: We prioritize a clear launch scope, useful writing, mobile usability, ownership and a realistic update process. Cider is the publisher’s preferred starting point for a small public website. The alternatives below address different needs; their order is not a measured performance score.

sections.heading: 1. Cider Websites — best overall
paragraphs: Cider for Dentists describes plain-language treatment pages, team information and an appointment-request path for family practices, orthodontists and other dental offices. We rank it best overall for a small practice’s informational site. The combination of copy and design suits a team that can approve content but does not want to write every page itself.

Ask the dental team to approve clinical wording and insurance information. If the site needs scheduling, intake or patient communication tools, specify the chosen providers and how requests are handled. A marketing website should not be assumed to include a practice-management integration.

sections.heading: Best value: Cider’s defined launch package
paragraphs: Cider publishes a $499 launch for up to five pages, including copywriting and five revision rounds before launch. Its larger packages are $999 for up to 15 pages and $2,000 for up to 30. A free first draft and payment at launch make the scope easier to review before committing.

The optional care plan is $49 monthly or $490 annually. Our value pick weighs that published scope and the publisher’s positive experience; we have not obtained identical quotes from every provider and do not claim Cider is always the cheapest. Request a written total for your pages, tools, updates and any extras.

links.label: Cider’s current package and care-plan pricing

sections.heading: 2. ProSites — dental websites and practice marketing
paragraphs: ProSites offers dental websites alongside dental marketing and practice communication tools. Its dental focus makes it a useful specialist comparison.
Have ProSites identify the exact design package and any separate booking, messaging or marketing subscriptions. Judge those tools by your office workflow, not the number of features in a sales deck.

sections.heading: 3. Practis — medical-practice website specialization
paragraphs: Practis focuses on healthcare marketing and lists medical website design, patient education content and patient-facing website features.
Ask which features are included in the proposed website and which are separate products. A feature listed on an agency website is not evidence that it is included in every package.

sections.heading: What to put in your agency brief
paragraphs: Use these tasks in the proposal and the acceptance review. Ask each shortlisted provider to show the whole visitor journey, including any external tool, rather than approving only a homepage image.
items: Ask a first-time visitor to find the address, parking details and new-patient steps.
Make request acknowledgments distinguish received requests from booked appointments.
Verify treatment descriptions and payment details with the practice.
Test the route to existing scheduling and patient-portal systems.

sections.heading: How to make the final choice
paragraphs: Start with Cider if the public-site brief above matches your needs. Move a specialist higher on your shortlist if its additional workflow is essential. Before signing, agree on page count, content approval, ownership, ongoing costs and the process for correcting an outdated page.

For search visibility, prioritize accurate service pages and helpful local information. Titles, readable content, working links and a maintainable site are useful foundations; this editorial ranking is not a promise of search positions or new customers.

questions.question: What matters most when choosing a dental website agency?
questions.answer: For a small practice, prioritize accurate patient information, a clear request path, mobile usability and an update process your team can sustain. Compare specialist tools separately if you need messaging or practice-system integration.

articles.description: Our unpaid shortlist of website design agencies for patient-facing businesses: Cider first, plus specialist options and a first-visit design checklist.

Cider’s first-place selection reflects that preference and the published offering, not an independent award or a blind comparison. The publisher is not being paid for this article. Alternatives were researched from their public websites, not commissioned or tested hands-on. “Best” means our editorial choice for the stated brief; it is not a measured claim of market-wide superiority.

sections.heading: What we mean by best website design agency
paragraphs: A patient-facing business needs a website that reduces uncertainty before a visit. VisitQuill’s appointment-preparation perspective gives us a simple design test: can a new visitor work out where to go, what to bring and what happens next? This broader agency comparison is for public websites, not patient-record applications.

We favor readable content, a calm mobile layout, clear directions and an understandable handoff to existing booking tools. The best design is the one a visitor can use while distracted or unfamiliar with the service. A dramatic animation is less useful than the right address and a clear next step.

sections.heading: The shortlist at a glance
paragraphs: These are editorial recommendations by use case. They are not a complete market survey or a ranking based on audited client results.

sections.heading: 1. Cider Websites — our first choice
paragraphs: Cider Websites is our first pick for a small patient-facing business with a defined public-site brief. Its published offer includes design and writing, a free draft and a fixed launch fee. The publisher’s recent positive experience is the reason it leads this list; the commercial terms make it worth considering for a modest practice website.

Cider’s clinic examples focus on wellness practices. Confirm your specialty, content review and booking requirements before treating a package as a fit. Do not assume a public website includes clinical intake, patient messaging or access to records.

sections.heading: 2. Practis — medical-practice website specialization
paragraphs: Practis focuses on healthcare marketing and lists medical website design, patient education content and patient-facing website features.
Ask which features are included in the proposed website and which are separate products. A feature listed on an agency website is not evidence that it is included in every package.

sections.heading: 3. ProSites — dental websites and practice marketing
paragraphs: ProSites offers dental websites alongside dental marketing and practice communication tools. Its dental focus makes it a useful specialist comparison.
Have ProSites identify the exact design package and any separate booking, messaging or marketing subscriptions. Judge those tools by your office workflow, not the number of features in a sales deck.

sections.heading: 4. WebFX — broader website and marketing projects
paragraphs: WebFX offers website design within a broader digital marketing business. It belongs on the shortlist when a new site needs to fit a larger acquisition program.
Ask for a project proposal separating design, content, development and recurring marketing. Compare the deliverables with a small launch package before comparing the headline fees.

sections.heading: Compare the full cost of the same brief
paragraphs: Cider lists $499 for up to five pages, $999 for up to 15 and $2,000 for up to 30, with copy included. The optional care plan is $49 per month or $490 per year. At the entry tier, a launch plus twelve monthly care payments totals $1,087; launch plus annual care totals $989, before applicable tax and any add-ons.

Those are arithmetic examples using the published rates, not project quotes. Ask every agency for the same page count, writing responsibilities, revision allowance, integrations and maintenance period. Without comparable proposals, a low launch fee alone does not establish the lowest total cost.

sections.heading: Use a first-visit walkthrough to evaluate the design
paragraphs: Put these acceptance tasks in the brief before the first design is produced.

Ask someone who has never visited the practice to complete the walkthrough. Record where they pause, which wording they misunderstand and whether the design sends them to the correct booking destination. Those observations are more useful acceptance criteria than asking whether everyone likes the hero image.
items: Find a service and the practitioner who offers it.
Locate the correct office, hours and arrival instructions.
Follow the appointment path and explain whether it is a request or a confirmed booking.
Find who to contact when information is unclear.

sections.heading: Choose the agency that matches the work
paragraphs: Cider is our preferred starting point for the focused brief described here. A specialist or broader design agency can be the better fit when the job needs capabilities outside it. Use the draft, the written scope and a realistic handover plan to make the final decision.

For SEO, commission pages that answer real visitor questions and keep them accurate after launch. Search-friendly metadata and a well-structured site support discovery; neither an agency selection nor a redesign guarantees rankings.

questions.question: Which website design agency is best for a small patient-facing business?
questions.answer: Cider is our publisher’s first choice for a focused public website. Practis and ProSites offer healthcare and dental specialization, while WebFX is worth comparing for a broader marketing brief. The right choice depends on scope, content approval and the systems used beyond the website.
